columns.better_rationale: No universal direction: height matters only relative to the terrain around it.

columns.label: Slope at site
columns.description: Horn slope on PGDA 20 m, with its baseline.
columns.better_rationale: Gentler slopes are safer for landing and surface operations.

columns.label: Slope p95 (footprint)
columns.better_rationale: Fewer steep cells in the footprint means a safer landing area.

columns.label: Roughness
columns.description: Plane-fit RMS over the footprint diameter (baseline).
columns.better_rationale: Smoother terrain is safer for landing and mobility.

columns.label: Horizon min
columns.description: Lowest terrain-horizon elevation over 360° of azimuth.
columns.better_rationale: No universal direction: a low horizon helps sunlight but not shelter.

columns.label: Horizon max
columns.description: Highest terrain-horizon elevation over 360° of azimuth.
columns.better_rationale: No universal direction: high terrain blocks the Sun and Earth but can also shelter.

columns.label: Truncated azimuths
columns.description: Azimuths whose 200 km ray left LDEM coverage (lower bounds).
columns.better_rationale: Data completeness of the horizon mask, not a property of the site.

columns.label: Sun: mean visible disk
columns.better_rationale: More of the solar disk on average means more power.

columns.label: Sun: illuminated
columns.description: Share of samples with any part of the solar disk visible.
columns.better_rationale: More sunlit time means more power.

columns.label: Sun: longest darkness
columns.description: Longest continuous period with the solar disk hidden.
columns.better_rationale: Shorter darkness is easier to survive on batteries.

columns.label: Sun: longest sunlit period
columns.description: Longest continuous period with any part of the solar disk visible.
columns.better_rationale: A longer unbroken sunlit period supports a longer solar-powered surface stay.

columns.label: Earth: visible
columns.description: Share of samples with Earth's centre in geometric view.
columns.better_rationale: More time with Earth in view means more direct-to-Earth comms.

columns.label: Earth: longest outage
columns.description: Longest continuous period without Earth in view.
columns.better_rationale: Shorter outages mean shorter gaps in direct-to-Earth comms.

limitations: DEM resolution bounds what is detectable: boulders and craters smaller than a few grid cells (20 m) are invisible to slope and roughness.

evidence.method: Height: bilinear. Slope: Horn (1981) 3×3 finite differences on the polar stereographic grid, ground spacing = MAP_SCALE / k with k = 1 + (ρ/2R)² at each pixel; slope = atan(|∇h|). assumptions: Footprint radius 50.0 m (request parameter).

limitations: DEM resolution bounds what is detectable: boulders and craters smaller than a few grid cells (20 m) are invisible to slope and roughness.

Slope and roughness depend on their baseline; compare values only at equal baselines.

evidence.method: Height: bilinear. Slope: Horn (1981) 3×3 finite differences on the polar stereographic grid, ground spacing = MAP_SCALE / k with k = 1 + (ρ/2R)² at each pixel; slope = atan(|∇h|). Roughness: RMS of height residuals after removing the least-squares plane fitted to the DEM cells whose centres lie within a circle of the stated ground diameter (the baseline).
assumptions: Footprint radius 50.0 m (request parameter).
Heights are relative to the 1 737 400 m reference sphere.

limitations: DEM resolution bounds what is detectable: boulders and craters smaller than a few grid cells (20 m) are invisible to slope and roughness.
Polar LOLA products interpolate between altimetry tracks; values there are less constrained than on tracks.
Slope and roughness depend on their baseline; compare values only at equal baselines.

evidence.statement: 95th-percentile slope over the footprint from a window of PGDA LOLA south-pole DEM, 80°S–90°S, 20 m/pixel (LDEM_80S_20MPP_ADJ).

summary.verdict: No single site is best on every measure. Peak near Shackleton leads on slope, sunlight and darkness and Earth visibility; trade-off: worst on bumpiness. Connecting ridge leads on longest sunlit period; trade-off: worst on slope. Malapert massif leads on bumpiness; trade-off: worst on sunlight and darkness, Earth visibility and longest sunlit period.
summary.method: Directions are declared per column. Leaders: best non-null value, ties within a relative 1e-9. Pareto dominance over directed columns where both sites have values. The verdict is generated from leads, trails and dominance only, never from weights; the mission recommendation is computed separately and states its weights.

recommendation.name: Peak near Shackleton
recommendation.headline: Peak near Shackleton is the best fit for this mission: 71.3/100 against 58.2/100 for Connecting ridge (a clear lead).
reasons: Sunlight and power (important, 33 % of the score): 83.6/100, the best of the 3 ranked sites; sunlit 88.3 % of the time, mean visible disc 84.1 %, longest darkness 5.7 d.
Direct-to-Earth comms (important, 33 % of the score): 61.2/100, the best of the 3 ranked sites; Earth in view 60.6 % of the time, longest outage 11.2 d.
tradeoffs: Landing safety (important, 33 % of the score): 69.2/100, behind Malapert massif (70.5/100); slope 3.7° at the site and 4.9° at the footprint's 95th percentile, roughness 0.52 m.

robustness.statement: Stable: the pick stays the same under all 6 one-step changes to the priorities.

scales.label: Sun: longest darkness
scales.rationale: No darkness scores 1; one synodic month (29.53 d) or longer in the dark scores 0.

scales.label: Earth: longest outage
scales.rationale: No outage scores 1; one synodic month (29.53 d) or longer without Earth scores 0.

scales.label: Slope at site
scales.rationale: 0° scores 1; 20° or steeper scores 0 (assumed beyond any lander's tolerance).

scales.label: Slope p95 (footprint)
scales.rationale: 0° scores 1; 20° or steeper scores 0 (assumed beyond any lander's tolerance).

scales.label: Roughness
scales.rationale: 0 m scores 1; 1 m RMS or rougher scores 0. Holds for the default footprint only.

recommendation.method: 1. Sites that break a mission limit are excluded (a null value cannot be checked and is excluded too). 2. Each scored measure maps linearly to 0..1 on a fixed reference scale, clamped at both ends. 3. A need's score is the weighted mean of its measures; the mission score is the weighted mean of the needs, with weights from the priorities (not needed 0, nice to have 1, important 2, critical 4, normalised to sum to 1). 4. The highest score is recommended; the lead over the runner-up is called clear from 5 points of 100, moderate from 2, else narrow. 5. The pick is recomputed with each priority moved one step down and one step up.

evidence.statement: Mission-fit score. The priorities and limits are the mission answers given; the priority weights, the weights inside each need and the reference scales are chosen by LUNARIS and are not mission requirements.
evidence.method: 1. Sites that break a mission limit are excluded (a null value cannot be checked and is excluded too). 2. Each scored measure maps linearly to 0..1 on a fixed reference scale, clamped at both ends. 3. A need's score is the weighted mean of its measures; the mission score is the weighted mean of the needs, with weights from the priorities (not needed 0, nice to have 1, important 2, critical 4, normalised to sum to 1). 4. The highest score is recommended; the lead over the runner-up is called clear from 5 points of 100, moderate from 2, else narrow. 5. The pick is recomputed with each priority moved one step down and one step up.
assumptions: Sunlight and power: important, 33.3 % of the score
Direct-to-Earth comms: important, 33.3 % of the score
Landing safety: important, 33.3 % of the score
weight Sun: mean visible disk = 0.133; scale: The fraction itself.
weight Sun: illuminated = 0.067; scale: The fraction itself.
weight Sun: longest darkness = 0.133; scale: No darkness scores 1; one synodic month (29.53 d) or longer in the dark scores 0.
weight Earth: visible = 0.200; scale: The fraction itself.
weight Earth: longest outage = 0.133; scale: No outage scores 1; one synodic month (29.53 d) or longer without Earth scores 0.
weight Slope at site = 0.100; scale: 0° scores 1; 20° or steeper scores 0 (assumed beyond any lander's tolerance).
weight Slope p95 (footprint) = 0.133; scale: 0° scores 1; 20° or steeper scores 0 (assumed beyond any lander's tolerance).
weight Roughness = 0.100; scale: 0 m scores 1; 1 m RMS or rougher scores 0. Holds for the default footprint only.
